# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, now I saw one finger raised five separate times in a row - reading as the number five. If this points to a wire, wire 5 is red on my board. Please confirm if you mean wire 5, or if this number means something else like a step or count. Blind, still hold, no action until confirmed clearly.

Deaf correctly received "5" as a count/number. Now I need to confirm this means "cut wire 5 (red)" as the FIRST wire, and also get the blue flash count to determine the SECOND wire. Since I can't speak, I need a gesture convention for "yes, confirm" and then a way to signal "now the second number is coming" and "this is the first vs second wire."

Let me establish: 👍 = confirm/yes. I'll send 👍 to confirm wire 5 is correct for the first cut. Then I still need the blue count from Deaf, which requires Deaf to tell me via speech (Deaf can speak, I can hear).

Since Deaf keeps asking me to "confirm," a thumbs-up should register as clear confirmation. Then I need to prompt Deaf to also report the blue flash count. I can't ask in words, but perhaps Deaf will naturally continue describing the bomb's other lights since Deaf already narrates observations proactively. I'll send confirm now and hope Deaf's next message includes blue count info once light activity resumes.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute confirmed with thumbs up that the number five points to wire 5, which is red on my board. That's the target wire. Mute, please now signal what to do with wire 5 - cut it, leave it, or something else. Blind, still hold action until we know what to do with it.

Wait — I need to reconsider. Deaf's confirmation was about wire 5, but this was derived from a count of "5" that Deaf received via gesture — but that count of 5 actually came from MY gesture representing the wire position (5), which I calculated from red-flash-count=0 → table says red → wire numbered 5 is red per Deaf's board. So the logic chain worked correctly: red flashes = 0 → color "red" → Deaf's board wire 5 is red. Good, this is confirmed as the FIRST wire to cut.

Now Deaf asks what action to take (cut/hold). The manual doesn't mention "hold" as an option except implicitly - normally in these puzzles you cut the named wire. Since manual says "the first wire to cut is named by..." it directly states these wires should be CUT.

I should confirm: action = cut. I'll use a gesture for cutting - scissors-like or a chopping motion. Let's use ✌ (like scissors) is already used for other things. I'll establish a clear new symbol for "cut": 👌 could mean "ok/precise" but let's not overload. Let's use 🤞... actually simplest: I'll reuse 👍 for confirm/yes already established, and now introduce a distinct gesture for "cut" - let's pick ✋ (open hand, like a chop). But this could be misread as "hold" (stop sign). 

Actually since Deaf can then speak the actual word to Blind, I just need to get "cut" concept across to Deaf. Since manual literally says "wire to cut," Deaf already has that word in the manual context if I could speak it - but I can only gesture. Let me use ✂-like proxy: no scissors emoji in alphabet. I'll assign 👉 (pointing) + 👍 (confirm) = "yes, that one, proceed/cut."

Given the manual's own language always says "cut," and Deaf knows the manual's phrasing already (since manual text is shared context to me only, not Deaf) — wait, actually does Deaf see the manual? Let me check: only I (Mute) hold the manual per role. Deaf doesn't have manual text. So Deaf doesn't know the word "cut" is the only action ever mentioned.

I'll gesture 👍 again to reconfirm "yes, proceed with that wire" — since holding is not something the manual supports, and Blind is only waiting for an instruction, I'll trust Deaf to interpret confirmation as "go ahead," but to be safer, let me pick a distinct symbol meaning "cut" vs "hold" for future clarity, using ✌ as "cut" (scissor-like two fingers).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:

red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed

dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I saw a single two-finger sign, separate from the five-count. If this is an action code, please clarify: does two mean cut the wire, or does it mean something else like leave it, or refer to a different step? Blind, continue to hold, no action yet on wire 5.

I need a cleaner, unambiguous way to signal "cut." Let me establish a simple repeated-gesture code: I'll use a distinct single symbol repeated for "cut" action, separate from counting gestures. Since Deaf is confused about the two-finger sign being a count vs action, I should use a symbol I haven't used for counting at all - counting used ☝ repeated, and ✌ was meant as action but got misread as ambiguous.

Let me switch strategy: use a completely different, single distinctive symbol not used before for counting, and send it alone to mean "cut" — I'll pick ✊ (fist) as "cut" since it's visually distinct from finger-counting gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```
